body.p: JALv3 procedures and functions may declare trailing parameters as optional and give them a default value. A call may then omit any trailing run of those arguments.
body.codeblock:
PROCEDURE blink(BYTE IN pin, OPTIONAL WORD IN delay_ms DEFAULT 500) IS ... END PROCEDURE
blink(3) -- delay_ms = 500 blink(3, 1000) -- delay_ms = 1000

ul.li: OPTIONAL parameters must come after all required parameters. A required parameter after an optional one is an error.
Only IN parameters may be optional. A default on an OUT or IN OUT parameter is an error.
DEFAULT is mandatory and must be a constant expression: a literal, a constant, or constant arithmetic. The value is typed by the parameter.
Optional parameters work with BIT, every integer width, VOLATILE formals, and open arrays whose default is a string literal.
Direct calls only. Function-pointer calls keep the full-arity rule, and pseudo-variable routines ('get and 'put) do not support optional parameters at all.

body.p: An open array may declare a literal default. The literal is materialized once, and COUNT inside the callee sees its length:
body.codeblock:
PROCEDURE tag(OPTIONAL BYTE IN txt[] DEFAULT "n/a") IS print_byte_dec(serial_data, BYTE(COUNT(txt))) END PROCEDURE
tag() -- prints 3 tag("custom") -- prints 6
body.p: A string literal passed to a STRING or STRING[N] formal is staged into a compiler string cell, so any length up to the capacity compiles. An optional string parameter may also use a string literal as its default.

section.title: The empty-string sentinel
section.p: When a call needs to supply a later optional argument while leaving an earlier one at its default, an empty string literal can stand in for the omitted value. Passing "" to a non-string optional parameter means omitted, and the declared default is used. The sentinel works in the middle of an argument list and for open-array defaults.
section.codeblock:
PROCEDURE draw(BYTE IN x, OPTIONAL BYTE IN colour DEFAULT 1, OPTIONAL BIT IN bold DEFAULT FALSE) IS ... END PROCEDURE
draw(10, "", TRUE) -- colour defaults to 1, bold is TRUE
section.p: Only the empty literal is the sentinel. A string of two or more characters remains a type error, and a one-character literal keeps its long-standing char-code meaning, so "x" passes 120 to a byte parameter. Required parameters never accept the sentinel, and STRING-typed formals receive "" as a real empty string.

body.p: Optional arguments are filled in by the caller: the compiler emits an ordinary full-arity call, so the mechanism is identical on every target.
